topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by outlining its main objectives regarding cancer evolution, cellular predisposition, and the tumor microenvironment.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic mechanisms of clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how pre-malignant cells acquire competitive advantages and transform through stepwise genetic mutations and epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Cell of origin and stem cell hierarchies in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore whether tumors initiate within tissue-specific stem cells or differentiated progenitors, examining how stemness hierarchies influence malignant progression.

topics.label: Role of the microenvironment and inflammation in cancer progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate that both incipient and established tumors depend on non-cell-autonomous environmental signals to promote and sustain malignant growth.

topics.label: Technological methods for studying tumor evolution and microenvironments
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the experimental and computational technologies used to reconstruct mutation timing and map spatial cellular interactions in human tumors.

topics.label: Integrative evolutionary model of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes the lecture's core themes into an integrated framework of cancer as a multi-step evolutionary process shaped by intrinsic and extrinsic factors.

topics.label: Closing remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on cancer therapies.
